recipes.name: Broccoli and Tortellini Salad
ingredients_raw: 3 heads fresh broccoli, cut into florets

steps.text: Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium high heat until evenly brown. Drain, crumble and set aside.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook tortellini in boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente. Drain, and rinse under cold water.
In a small bowl, mix together mayonnaise, sugar and vinegar to make the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine broccoli, tortellini, bacon, raisins, sunflower seeds and red onion. Pour dressing over salad, and toss.

raw_recipe.headline: Broccoli and Tortellini Salad
raw_recipe.description: Broccoli keeps very good company in this wonderful salad. There's fresh cheese tortellini, bacon, raisins, sunflower seeds, broccoli florets, red onion, and a sweet and sour mayonnaise dressing tossed in for good measure.

review.reviewBody: I love this salad, but I find the the dry tortellini (found on the shelf in the pasta aisle) holds up so much better than the refrigerated (and it is a much better bang for your buck). I used Barilla cheese tortellini, and it was absolutely superb!

Delish! Make sure to do these few things, and your salad will be Fabulous. 1.) Blanch brocolli peices in almost boiling water for about 1 minute, scoop out and put in ice water to shock and produce a beautiful green 2.) toast sunflower seeds 3.) if you use frozen tortelinni, cook for only 2-3 minutes in not-quite-boiling water- they will be done enough, any longer and they will be mushy and fall apart 4.) make 4 times the dressing called for, use a combo of miricle whip and mayo and only 1/2 cup sugar. Lastly, mix pasta, broccoli, craisins and 2/3 of the dressing the day before and let it marinate! Top with the rest of the dressing, seeds and bacon (i didn't use onion) right before serving. Your family will love this!

This recipe is wonderful! I made a couple of small changes to suit our tastes. First, I steamed the broccoli very briefly to keep it crisp. As others have noted, the dressing is on the sweet side so I only used 2 TBS of sugar. Then I found there was not quite enough dressing so I made another batch and used half of it. It was perfect (and not at all runny). Instead of 1 cup of sunflower seeds I used 3/4 cup of sunflower kernels and 1/2 cup of roughly chopped cashews. I also used dried cranberries because I'm not a fan of raisins. I cooked 8 strips of bacon and found I could have used the whole pound so I sprinkled some Hormel Real Bacon Bits on top. Minor changes to an excellent recipe. Thank you for sharing AFMC!

I used a spinach and cheese tortellini and a pre-packaged salad topping mixture of walnuts and cranberries. Forgot to add the bacon to hubs' portion, but he didn't seem to miss it. I made the dressing the night before, so it had time to sit. I added the chopped broccoli to the pasta the last few minutes of boil time. Then tossed in some shaved carrots the last minute for added color. Rinsed in cold water, drained very well and then tossed with the dressing. Such a nice, simple salad! Will do again!

This was a great recipe. I blanched the broccoli for 30 seconds exactly. Any longer and it would have been too soft. The blanching really brought out the beautiful green in the broccoli. After blanching, I soaked the florets in ice water. Per another suggestion, I made 1.5 times the dressing, added 1/3 of it right after I made the salad. Placed everything in a Ziploc in the fridge for a few hours and before I served it, I added the remaining dressing. I didn't 1.5 times the sugar in the dressing but kept it at 1/2 a cup sine I don't like things super sweet. I also needed to add some salt to the salad after I made it and it could be because I didn't salt the water enough when I cooked the tortellini. I also only used 1/4 of a purple onion. it seems like a whole one would have been too much and it could be because the onion I had was on the larger size. Everyone complimented me and it was all gone! This is going to be my new go-to potluck dish!

Had a package of tortellini I wanted to use up along with some broccoli. This was a very good combination. I added the broccoli to the last 2 minutes of the boiling tortellini water to make the green "pop" in color. I would do this again. Make your dressing up ahead of time so that the sugar has time to melt into the mayonnaise, stirring often. I used all the ingredients, but changed the order a little bit. After the dressing was well blended, about an hour I added it to the salad, withholding the sunflower seeds and bacon. I added those right before serving because I wanted them to still have some crunch. Good salad and would make it again.

Lovely recipe that I modified slightly. Used 20oz of the dry tortellini and blanched the broccoli in the pasta water at the end of cooking for 2mins. Used 3/4 cup mayo with 1/4 cup sugar and 3TBLS of cider vinegar. Mixed a the dressing, veggies,pasta and craisins together and chilled over night. Mixed in the bacon and seeds right before serving to my co-workers that loved it. What little that was left tasted even better the next day!! Thank you AMFC

I brought this to a potluck and it was a huge hit! I followed other reviewers tips and blanched the broccoli and onion for 2 minutes, divided the raisins into half raisins and craisins, toasted the sunflower seeds and cut the sugar in half. I also added a head of broccoli, cut the cider vinegar in half and doubled the amount of dressing. I couldn't find dry tortellini in the store so I used fresh and it worked out perfectely. Thank you for this recipe I will definitely be making this again!

A huge hit! I did use less than 1/4c sugar, 3/4c mayo and 2Tbsp. cider vinegar, we mixed everything but the pasta and bacon and left sitting for a few hours; then added the last two before serving. It was perfect for my family; the girls devoured the broccoli "trees".

This broccoli salad is fantastic. I followed the advice of many reviewers before more me and I thank them all for their tips. 1) Only cooked the refrigerated tortellini for 2-3 mins. 2) Blanched the broccoli in super hot water for 1 minute. 3) Double the amount of salad dressing!!! This last bullet is imperative. I put half the dressing on the night before and the other half just before serving it. Also, add sugar to the dressing in baby steps (1 T. at a time) and then taste test it. I personally didn't add nearly the amount of sugar the recipe called for but that is just personal taste. I waited to add the sunflower seeds and the crumbled bacon to the salad until the last minute as well. I was worried that they would get soggy overnight and the crunchy texture is part of the salad's uniqueness in my opinion. This recipe went immediately into my favorite folder!! Thanks AMFC for sharing it!

I, like many, have made this several times. 
Here's what I can share - blanche the broccoli in the same pan you're going to cook the pasta in - UNCUT, and quench in the large bowl you'll be mixing in. This will save the water to cook the tortellini in, and makes it easier to blanche and remove the broccoli from the water. I place a towel in the drainer and set the broccoli in it and then start the tortellini. As the tort's are cooking, I move the broccoli heads to a towel to finish draining. Easier to cut this way too! After I quench, and as the broccoli heads are drying, I clean out the large bowl. (This is all while the bacon is cooking on low/medium heat and I am mixing the dressing ingredients.)
For the dressing, I take the mayo to 1C, and also use 1/2C Miracle Whip style dressing. Sugar is 1/2C. Apple cider vinegar is at 6 teaspoons - RAW apple cider vinegar. 
I mix all but 1/2C of dressing with everything but the tortellini (and the bacon has been cut into small pieces with kitchen shears). I then gently toss the frozen tri-color torts and place in the fridge, covered. 
Just before serving, mix in the rest of the dressing and have some copies of this recipe to hand out. 
It is that good.
I like a little extra bacon!!!
I make this often! It's delicious!!!

I made this recipe and took the advice of some of the reviewers and used 1 cup of mayonnaise instead of 1/2. It was wonderful. The next day, it was a tad dry and I added about 1/4 cup of the Mayo, sugar, vinegar sauce and it brought it right back to life. This dish will be a staple for me going forward. Wonderful dish!

Have made this recipe for years and changed it up sometimes due to not having raisins used craisins used pumpkin or pepita seeds if don't have sunflower, added shredded Parmesan and used olive oil only with salt and pepper if out of mayo but the basics cheese tortellini and broccoli make it great regardless if other changes are made. A real keeper. A Family and crowd favorite.

This is very good and was easy to throw together. It is sweet, so if you don't like your broccoli salad sweet, decrease the sugar a little. I made extra "dressing" because I like a little more sauce. It tastes even better the next day.
No sunflower seeds and big bites of onions. Yummy

This salad was okay. I followed the recipe and the dressing came out very thin and watery. I drained the tortellini and the broccoli pretty well. The dressing had a good taste to it but overall it was disappointing.
Easy and delicious! Just the way I like it!
